issues.description: ValueError on unsupported delimiter contradicts type hint and Raises docstring
issues.detail: When an unsupported delimiter is passed, the method raises ValueError, but the function's documented Raises section only mentions HTTPBadRequest (for required params missing or transforms raising ValueError). A programmer-error ValueError raised from get_param_as_list is undocumented and may also be intercepted by Falcon's framework error handlers in surprising ways. Either document it explicitly under Raises, or validate the delimiter eagerly with a clearer exception type/message. The test test_get_param_as_list_unsupported_delimiter codifies this, but the docstring does not.

issues.description: Unsupported-delimiter validation only fires when param is a single string
issues.detail: The delimiter validity check lives inside `if delimiter is not None and isinstance(items, str):`. If the same param is sent multiple times (so `items` is already a list), or if the param is missing entirely, an invalid delimiter like ';' is silently accepted with no error. This makes the validation non-deterministic from the caller's perspective — a misconfigured delimiter will only surface for some requests. Validate the delimiter argument once at the top of the function, independent of the param's presence/shape.

issues.description: Overload signatures use `delimiter: str | None = None` literal default instead of `= ...`
issues.detail: All six @overload stubs were updated with `delimiter: str | None = None`, but PEP 484 / typing convention for overloads is to use `= ...` (ellipsis) as the default placeholder. Mixing a literal default into overload stubs is harmless to type checkers but is inconsistent with the rest of the overloads in this file (which use `store: StoreArg = ...`, `default: ... = ...`). This is a stylistic inconsistency that reviewers in this codebase typically flag.

issues.description: Interaction with `transform` argument is unspecified and untested
issues.detail: `get_param_as_list` accepts a `transform` callable applied to each item. The new delimiter-split path produces items from `str.split`, which are then passed (or not) through the rest of the method's processing. The PR adds no test covering `delimiter=` together with `transform=` — e.g., `get_param_as_list('ids', transform=int, delimiter='|')`. Given Type3_Latent_Candidate classification, this is exactly the kind of interaction that quietly breaks. Add at least one test combining delimiter with a transform that raises ValueError to confirm HTTPBadRequest is still produced.

If the param value is the empty string (e.g., `?names=`) and `keep_blank_qs_values` is on, `''.split('|')` returns `['']`, so the caller gets a list containing one empty string. Similarly `?names=a||b` with `delimiter='|'` yields `['a', '', 'b']`. The docstring claims `keep_blank_qs_values` has no effect on secondary splitting, but does not specify whether empty fragments are preserved or stripped. The behavior is testable but not tested; document and test it (the OpenAPI styles generally drop empty fragments, which is the opposite of what `str.split` does).

issues.description: Delimiter dict design conflates 'characters' and 'style names' in one namespace
issues.detail: `_PARAM_VALUE_DELIMITERS` mixes literal characters (',', '|', ' ') with OpenAPI style names ('pipeDelimited', 'spaceDelimited') in a single flat dict. This works but couples two concerns: validating which characters are allowed and translating OpenAPI style aliases. A cleaner design would be a small alias map (`'pipeDelimited' -> '|'`, `'spaceDelimited' -> ' '`) plus a frozenset of allowed final characters. The current dict also means a future addition of 'tabDelimited' requires touching the same structure as raw-character validation.

issues.description: Multi-character delimiter strings are silently rejected without a clear error
issues.detail: Any string not in `_PARAM_VALUE_DELIMITERS` triggers the generic 'Unsupported delimiter value' error. A user passing `delimiter='\t'` or `delimiter=';'` gets the same message as someone passing `delimiter='pipedelimited'` (case typo). Consider distinguishing 'unknown OpenAPI style' from 'unsupported character'. Also, the error lists all supported keys including raw characters which is fine but a bit noisy.

issues.description: No test for the `delimiter=None` default (regression guard for existing callers)
issues.detail: All new tests pass an explicit delimiter. There is no test asserting that `get_param_as_list('x')` (no delimiter) behaves identically to before — i.e., that adding the parameter is a pure additive change. The existing test suite presumably covers this, but a single explicit regression test for `delimiter=None` would lock in the contract.

issues.description: Docstring example uses percent-encoded pipe inconsistently with the 'after percent-decoding' note
issues.detail: The new doctest-style example shows `?colors=blue%7Cblack%7Cbrown` being split by `'pipeDelimited'`. The docstring earlier states that splitting happens after percent-decoding, which is correct, but the example only demonstrates the encoded case. A reader may infer that splitting depends on the encoded form. Adding a literal `?colors=blue|black|brown` example (or at least a comment) would clarify this.

issues.description: Test for auto_parse_qs_csv vs delimiter does not assert the comma path
issues.detail: `test_get_param_as_list_parse_qs_csv_vs_delimiter` sets `auto_parse_qs_csv=True` and checks pipe/space delimiters. It correctly verifies that when auto-CSV has already pre-split into a list, the delimiter is a no-op. But it does not test the same input with `delimiter=','` — which would be a useful symmetry test confirming both that the pre-split list short-circuits and that the original CSV behavior is preserved.

issues.description: Symbolic constants are magic strings rather than module-level constants
issues.detail: 'pipeDelimited' and 'spaceDelimited' are only discoverable via the docstring; there are no public constants like `falcon.PIPE_DELIMITED`. This is a minor API ergonomics gap — callers must hard-code strings that are easy to typo (e.g., 'pipeDelimeted'). For an additive feature this is acceptable, but exposing `PIPE_DELIMITED = 'pipeDelimited'` etc. would harden the API.

dissents.topic: Whether the delimiter allowlist is the right design

positions.position: A strict allowlist (only ',', '|', ' ', plus two OpenAPI aliases) is correct: it keeps the API aligned with the OpenAPI spec, prevents silly delimiters like ';' or '\n', and gives the maintainers a clear contract. The ValueError on unknown delimiter is a feature, not a bug.

The allowlist is over-restrictive. Falcon users often have legacy APIs using ';' or other separators. A more permissive approach would accept any single character and reserve the symbolic constants for OpenAPI styles only. The ValueError will frustrate users with valid use cases.

dissents.topic: Where to validate the delimiter argument

positions.position: Validate eagerly at function entry, before any branching on whether the param is present or already a list. Otherwise the same call site can succeed or fail depending on the request shape, which is a latent bug.

Validating only when needed (inside the str-only branch) keeps the hot path lean and avoids breaking callers who pass a 'wrong' delimiter for a param that happens to be a list. The current placement is defensible as 'validate only when you'd actually use it.'

dissents.topic: Should the function raise ValueError or HTTPBadRequest for invalid delimiter

positions.position: ValueError is appropriate because it's a programmer error (bad argument), not a client error. The caller passed a bad delimiter; the client did nothing wrong.

Other validation errors in get_param_* helpers raise HTTPBadRequest. Raising a bare ValueError leaks an implementation detail to the response handler and is inconsistent with the surrounding code, which catches ValueError from transforms and converts to HTTPBadRequest.

review.summary: The PR adds a `delimiter` keyword to `Request.get_param_as_list`, with reasonable docs, news fragment, overload updates, and tests. The core implementation is small and correct for the happy path. The main concerns are around edge cases: the unsupported-delimiter validation only triggers when the param value is a single string (so misconfigured delimiters silently pass for list-shaped or missing params), the ValueError is undocumented in the Raises section, interaction with `transform=` and with empty/blank values is untested, and overload stubs use literal defaults rather than the `...` convention used elsewhere in the file. None of these are merge-blocking, but several should be addressed before release. No P0 issues identified.
